title: AML runlog & prompt/quant notes — Sasha (quick log)
body:
Quick log for a few small experiments I ran while trying to triage generation quality drop after switching to q4_0 quant profile. Not polished — notes to self and quick commands.

2026-03-01 09:15 — context
- Goal: understand why chat completions with customer prompt set A (legal-summaries) are hallucinating dates more often after q4_0 deployment.
- Hypothesis: quantization noise in attention scores + KV-cache rounding leading to subtle token distribution shifts.
- Workstation: macbook + remote devbox (g4dn-like) via ssh -> run container with local build.

RUNS (local, minimal reproduction):
1) baseline (fp16)
cmd: python run_eval.py --model rwinf-open-13b --precision fp16 --prompt-set prompts/legal-set-A.json --temp 0.0 --max-tokens 150
results: 200 prompts, P(hallucinated_date)=0.035 (7/200).

2) q4_0 (fast quant)
cmd: python run_eval.py --model rwinf-open-13b-q4_0 --precision q4_0 --prompt-set prompts/legal-set-A.json --temp 0.0 --max-tokens 150
results: 200 prompts, P(hallucinated_date)=0.092 (18/200).
notes: significant jump. Qualitative: hallucinations biased toward near-future dates (2027-03) despite prompt referencing historical doc (2019).

3) q4_0 with temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.5)
- temp 0.0: 18/200
- temp 0.2: 20/200
- temp 0.5: 27/200 (higher temp amplifies noise)

4) q4_0 + kv-cache disabled (force recompute keys each step)
results: 12/200 -> partial improvement
thought: rounding in cached KV may accumulate; try higher fp fallback for kv-cache region.

Prompt variants tested (examples):
- Original: "Summarize the following clause and list the effective dates mentioned."
- Strong-fact anchor: "Only extract dates that explicitly appear in the text. If none, write "NONE"."
- Evidence-first: prefix with "From the excerpt below, quote any date tokens (YYYY or "March 3, 2019") verbatim."
Outcome: anchor prompts reduce hallucinations by ~40% for q4_0 but do not fully close gap. So prompting helps but hardware/quant still matters.

Quantization notes and quick config ideas:
- q4_0 default per-channel scale seems fine for weights, but attention softmax sensitive. Consider hybrid: q4_0 for FFN and MHA matmul, keep attention normalization/softmax at fp16 (or q8_hybrid).
- Try layer-wise higher-precision for first 6 layers (where date tokens often resolved early in context).
- Experiment: ladder quant profile (fp16 for norm + attention, q4_0 for linear layers).
- Also test symmetric vs asymmetric scaling for token-embedding matrix; small bias in embedding scale shifts token logits slightly.

Quick eval checklist (to run next):
- [ ] Run ladder quant profile with fp16 attention (script: tools/quant_profile.py --ladder) on 13B (target subset).
- [ ] Re-run prompt-set A + anchored prompts under ladder profile.
- [ ] Add a post-process filter that rejects dates not substring-matching original text (cheap immediate mitigation).
- [ ] Open perf ticket if ladder increases latency >10%: JIRA-ML-420.

Observations for infra/serving-runtime team (notes to mention in Slack):
- q4_0 rollout likely safe for many workloads, but specific structured-extraction prompts show regressions.
- Need a config knob in runtime to allow per-layer precision overrides for experimental rollouts.
- Also useful: an automated prompt suite that runs during quant rollout (small seeded evals).

Results snapshot (csv-like, quick):
config, temp, halluc_rate
fp16, 0.0, 0.035
q4_0, 0.0, 0.092
q4_0, 0.2, 0.100
q4_0, 0.5, 0.135
q4_0+no-kv, 0.0, 0.060
ladder-proposed, 0.0, TBD

Things I forgot to capture: exact seed values for runs (need to rerun with --seed 42). Also didn't capture per-prompt IDs for failing cases; will re-run failing subset with verbose logs.

Notes to self — reminders:
- Ping @Noah to get his eval harness that diff-checks token probabilities instead of just final strings.
- Save the 20 worst hallucination cases into /tmp/aml/debug/halluc-2026-03-01.txt and attach to Slack thread.
- If ladder reduces halluc_rate < 0.05, propose canary rollout to dedicated pool for 24h (need perf baseline).

Unresolved questions:
- Is the attention softmax implementation in the runtime performing any kernel-level approximations under q4_0? (ask infra team).
- Should we add an eval metric that measures "dates hallucination" specifically for legal prompts? Probably yes — quick regex-based metric.

Next steps (today):
1) Run ladder-profile quick experiment (expected run time ~45m).
2) Re-run top-20 failing prompts with seed and verbose logits.
3) Draft brief note for infra slack: describe per-layer precision knob and proposed canary.

End of quick log. Will update after ladder results.

-- Sasha
